name: hra-atlas-browser
title: HRA Atlas Browser — organ selector + model-count gradient + BioModels links
question:
Can we present the full HRA-3D model-coverage picture as an interactive
atlas: pick any of the 50 GLB-backed HRA organs, see its regions
demarcated and colored by how many mechanistic models are associated with
it, and browse straight to those BioModels?

study_card.goal: Cross the union of the name-synonym and SBML-annotation model catalogs (organ_index over 50 GLB organs x organ_to_models) into an atlas manifest, and render it as a self-contained three.js organ browser with a model-count color gradient and clickable BioModels.
study_card.mechanism: merge_catalogs(name-synonym corpus catalog, SBML-annotation catalog) -> build_atlas_manifest -> atlas.json (per-organ n_models_distinct + per-model provenance + BioModels links) -> viz/atlas/ three.js viewer (organ menu grouped by anatomical system, per-mesh EdgesGeometry outlines, viridis log-scaled count color, BioModels side panel with keyword search).
study_card.expected_result: All 50 organs selectable; 14 modeled organs colored by count (blood 51 brightest), 36 greyed; each organ's BioModels list links to ebi.ac.uk/biomodels.
study_card.main_expert_question: Is an organ-granularity model-count gradient a useful whole-atlas overview of where mechanistic modeling exists, given it cannot yet distinguish sub-regions within one organ?

biological_summary:
Mechanistic models cluster on a handful of organs (blood, pancreas, liver,
brain, intestine, heart) and leave most of the body's 3D anatomy unmodeled. The
Atlas Browser makes that distribution legible: the color gradient shows
where modeling effort has concentrated, and the greyed organs make the
modeling white-space visible at a glance.
readouts: atlas manifest: n_organs (50), n_modeled (14), n_models_distinct (167), n_models_total (229), max_models (51)

report.title: HRA Atlas Browser — 14/50 organs modeled, blood dominant
report.objective:
Present HRA-3D model coverage as an interactive organ browser with a
model-count gradient and BioModels links.
report.conclusion:
The atlas manifest covers all 50 GLB-backed HRA organs; 14 carry ≥1
model (blood 51, pancreas 47, liver 33, brain 29, intestine 18,
heart 11, lung 11, adipose 7, kidney 5, spleen 5, ovary 4, lymph node 3,
skin 3, urinary bladder 2), 36 are greyed. Counts are distinct models
from the union of name-synonym and SBML-annotation matching (167 distinct
/ 229 total). Each modeled organ links to its BioModels entries. The
gradient is organ-granularity: it shows where modeling exists across the
body but does not yet distinguish sub-regions within an organ.
report.caveat:
Coverage is organ-granularity — every sub-region of a modeled organ
inherits the organ's count, so the within-organ gradient is uniform.
True per-anatomical-structure counts are the fp-as-level-coverage
follow-up.

findings.statement:
The atlas manifest enumerates all 50 GLB-backed HRA organs and colors
the 14 modeled ones by model count (blood 51 max, 167 distinct models),
linking each to its BioModels entries — a whole-atlas overview of where
mechanistic modeling exists.

evidence.summary: 50 organs, 14 modeled (167 distinct / 229 total from the name-synonym union annotation union), max_models=51 (blood); 36 organs greyed (no models).

limitations: Organ-granularity gradient: sub-regions within an organ share the organ's count (no per-AS-node resolution yet).
Organ tagging is name-synonym-based (see hra-integration); untagged models may hide real organ relevance.

resolved_uncertainties: The full 50-organ GLB set is enumerable and renderable with a per-organ model-count gradient and BioModels links.
remaining_uncertainties: Can sub-region (AS-level) counts replace organ-granularity coloring? See fp-as-level-coverage.

followup_study_proposals.title: AS-level (sub-organ) model coverage in the Atlas Browser
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Color sub-regions within an organ by their own model count instead of inheriting the organ's count.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Parse SBML MIRIAM/Uberon annotations at anatomical-structure granularity, join to crosswalk AS nodes, and drive per-mesh color from per-node counts.
